site.name: King Wilhelm Mine
overview: King Wilhelm Mine is a documented historic gold-and-silver mine in Boulder County's Jamestown Mining District, preserved as a named mine on Boulder-area topographic mapping.

Geologic literature on Boulder County telluride ores records a distinctive mineral assemblage at King Wilhelm that includes native gold, petzite, chalcopyrite, molybdenite, pyrite and sphalerite, giving the site useful context beyond simple name-and-location identification.

timeline.text: King Wilhelm operated within the Jamestown district's gold-and-silver mining landscape. Available mapped records preserve the mine as an inactive historic working.
The Geological Society of America memoir Telluride Ores of Boulder County, Colorado documented King Wilhelm among Boulder County telluride-ore localities and recorded its mineral assemblage.
USGS-derived Boulder quadrangle mapping preserves a mine-level locality near 40.111652, -105.349159 for King Wilhelm.

moreHistory: The mine lies in the Jamestown Mining District, part of Boulder County's historically important precious-metal mining region. Modern locality records identify King Wilhelm as an inactive gold-and-silver mine at roughly 6,972 feet elevation.

Published Boulder County telluride-ore research records native gold and petzite at King Wilhelm together with chalcopyrite, molybdenite, pyrite and sphalerite. Remnant uses that source as site-specific geologic context without inferring unsupported production figures or exact operating dates.
The mapped mine-level point is used for identification only. Remnant does not claim that the coordinate is a field-surveyed surviving portal, shaft collar or other specific opening.
